status: DECIDED 2026-09-23 - no longer an open candidate
founding_population: MIXED - the most plural first-order unit in the survey. 2010 census: Han 50.5-54%; Tibetan 20.7-21%; Hui 16%; Tu (Monguor) 4%; Mongol 1.8%; Salar 1.8%. Total population 5,923,957 (2020)
why_excluded: Settled by the author: Qinghai joins The Northwest (13B) in the early era and passes into the Sinian Federation at unification. It is not its own region; it is not Tibetan
notes: DO NOT DRAW THIS AS A SEPARATE REGION AND DO NOT CROSS-HATCH IT ON ANY MAP. Retained as a row only to record why the decision went the way it did. THE CORE PROBLEM: QINGHAI IS HAN BY POPULATION AND TIBETAN BY TERRITORY; and the whole-subdivision rule forces one answer for both. Han are ~50-54% but concentrated in four cities in the northeast - Xining alone is ~28% of the province - while SIX OF EIGHT PREFECTURES ARE TIBETAN AUTONOMOUS PREFECTURES covering most of the 722300 km2. FOUR CANDIDATE HOMES: (1) TIBET as Amdo - weakened by the census; only 21% Tibetan; and Yongzheng administratively separated Qinghai from central Tibet in the 1720s; Amdowas historically identified as Amdowas rather than Tibetans and were sometimes closer to the Chinese than to U-Tsang. (2) ITS OWN REGION - the plural composition supports it; no group has a territorial claim that excludes the others. (3) THE SINIAN FEDERATION - but Qinghai was NEVER one of the Qing Eighteen; it was the Kokonor frontier domain. (4) THE NORTHWEST (13B) - THE NEW OPTION: the Ma clique held Gansu; Ningxia AND Qinghai 1919-1928 under Ma Qi and Ma Bufang; Qinghai is 16% Hui (~950000 people); and Xining orients toward Lanzhou. This is the only option with a documented precedent of Qinghai being governed WITH its neighbors rather than from Lhasa or Beijing. ALSO HOLDS: the Yellow River's source at Bayan Har; and Qarhan; China's largest potash source.
